title: Flamingo and Gated Cross-Attention for Few-Shot VLMs

questions.question: How does Flamingo add visual information to a frozen LLM while preserving the original text path at initialization?
options: Insert cross-attention with a residual gate initialized so tanh(alpha)=0.
Replace every text self-attention layer with image self-attention.
Append all visual patches to the vocabulary embedding table.
Unfreeze the LLM and let it relearn text behavior from image-caption pairs.
questions.explanation: Flamingo inserts cross-attention between frozen LLM blocks and adds it through y=tanh(α)·cross+x. At initialization α=0, so tanh(0)=0 and the pretrained text path is unchanged; replacing or unfreezing text layers would not preserve that behavior.

questions.question: For the residual y=tanh(alpha)*cross+x, what is y at initialization when alpha=0?
options: x+cross, because the residual adds both branches equally.
Exactly cross, because tanh(0)=1.
Exactly x, because tanh(0)=0.
Zero, because the gate suppresses the entire residual.
questions.explanation: Substituting α=0 gives y=tanh(0)·cross+x=0·cross+x=x. The gate suppresses only the new visual branch, not the residual text state; the cross output is not selected by itself.

questions.question: A Perceiver resampler uses K=64 learnable latents for images with either 196 or 900 patch tokens. What is the output length in both cases?
options: 196 visual tokens for either input patch count.
64 visual tokens for either input patch count.
900 visual tokens for either input patch count.
64 tokens only for the 196-patch image.
questions.explanation: The resampler uses K learnable latent queries to cross-attend over a variable number of image patches, so output length is K. With K=64, both 196- and 900-patch images produce 64 visual latents.

questions.question: In an interleaved sequence IMG0, text0, IMG1, text1, which image can a text1 token attend to under Flamingo's stated mask?
options: Only IMG1, the most recent preceding image.
Neither image, because text tokens use only causal self-attention.
Both IMG0 and IMG1, because all earlier images are visible.
Only IMG0, the first image in the whole prompt.
questions.explanation: The mask lets a text token attend to only the most recent image before it in the interleaved sequence. IMG1 is the latest image before text1; IMG0 is earlier and is not exposed to that token under this policy.

questions.question: A prompt contains several image-caption examples followed by a new image, and the model should use examples without a gradient step. Which architecture is designed for this?
options: A single-image Q-Former bridge with no interleaved sequence support.
Flamingo-style interleaved inputs with gated cross-attention.
A supervised image classifier trained on the prompt examples.
A zero-shot CLIP classifier that returns only a class similarity.
questions.explanation: Flamingo’s gated cross-attention lets a frozen language model condition on images interleaved with example text, preserving in-context learning without a gradient update at inference. A CLIP classifier returns similarity scores rather than a generated response.

questions.question: Images in a prompt have different resolutions and therefore different patch counts. What does the Perceiver resampler contribute?
options: It forces every image to have the same number of input patches before encoding.
It removes the image tokens and sends only the most recent caption.
It changes the frozen LLM's token embedding dimension per image.
It returns the same fixed number of visual latents for each image.
questions.explanation: Each image’s variable patch sequence is resampled into the same fixed K latent count before downstream use, giving a consistent visual-token shape. Resizing patches or changing the LLM embedding dimension is a different operation.
